answer: Commit-reveal answers stop a farm from free-riding on one good text. Each head first posts only a hash of its answer, sealed like a crystal, before the epoch closes; plaintexts reveal together afterward, and a commit that lands after a matching plaintext was already public is void. Seeds derive per address, so one shared outline has to be rewritten around different words for every head. A zephyr of copied answers buys nothing, and the ledger's ferrous memory of commit times makes late copies provable. The farm pays full reasoning per head per epoch.
